L10·N4507unmasked layer
This neuron is a context/register detector rather than a token detector: it fires on ordinary function words and sentence-final periods (e.g. "in", "can", "includes", ".", ",") inside generic explanatory/advisory web-copy or how-to prose, and is strongly suppressed at the same punctuation positions in concrete journalistic/narrative reporting (names, dates, sports scores).

L10·N5195unmasked layer

L10·N11581unmasked layer
This neuron fires on the small "linking" token that immediately precedes a concrete numeric value, identifier, or quoted spec value — e.g. " of" before a date/number, the colon after "Hardware ID", the space before "15 digits" or a coordinate, the opening quote before a value string — i.e. it marks the slot position where a specification value is about to be stated (it is suppressed when the same colon/period introduces ordinary prose instead).
